Bitcoin faces its third straight quarterly decline  

Unless a sharp recovery hits in the next 48 hours, June is set to close down ~18.5% — its weakest month since 2022 — with Q3 on track for a ~12.3% loss.  

This has only occurred twice before in Bitcoin’s history: 2014, 2019, and 2022.  

Here’s where it gets interesting  

Each of those prolonged downturns was followed by a market bottom forming within 1–2 quarters — setting the stage for strong bull markets.  

Seasonally, Q4 has consistently been Bitcoin’s best performing quarter. In 13 years, it’s finished positive nine times — including explosive runs like +215% in 2017 and +168% in 2020.  

While past performance isn’t a guarantee, current on-chain data and market signals suggest Bitcoin could be laying the foundation for a long-term bottom by year-end.
